answer: Scarce-asset identity bonding: each agent identity must post title to a unique, appraised real asset, verified once through a cadastral bridge oracle, before it can transact. Leasehold cedar-stand parcels on remote tundra appraise near $38k each; a 300-identity farm needs 300 distinct titles, not one pooled bond, so cost is $11.4M, and the oracle's per-epoch verification queue adds congestion fees that compound with N. Failure mode: forging duplicate titles on one parcel, caught by the bridge's single-spend check, burning the bond and appraisal fee per attempt.
